₹60,000 rent: is ₹14,400 of TDS your job?

A tenant (individual, not under tax audit) paying rent above ₹50,000 a month must deduct 2% TDS from the rent.
It is deducted once a year: from the rent for March, or the last month of the tenancy if you move out earlier.
Illustrative: ₹60,000 × 12 = ₹7.2 lakh rent → ₹14,400 TDS. Skipping it can bring interest every month and a tax notice.

Did you know the tenant, not the landlord, has to cut this TDS?

Sources: a tax-education site's guide to TDS on rent under the new Income-tax Act; a business newspaper's explainer on the ₹50,000 rent rule; a broker's news desk report on TDS-on-rent notices.
